sokkel-tui.note: The side panel on side-panel.base.rest.panel and the banner's slot on the banner's paints; not yet the shell's rule of 0.31.0, the status vocabulary or message ids.

summary: The frame every sokkel app has, on every target: the rail of places on the left, a thin top bar with the trail, search and palette, the page with its header as the one thing that scrolls, the settings dialog on its own route over the page, the status foot, and the states a page's read lands in.

sokkel-egui: crates/core/src/widgets/frame.rs (Shell; Rail, TopBar and StatusLine have their own specs, as PageHeader and PageState in page.rs do)

anatomy.rail: The app's places at the window's start: the rail (parts/rail). Below 768 it leaves the frame for the drawer.
anatomy.topBar: Over the content: the top bar (parts/top-bar), as tall as the rail's head, so the two read as one strip across the window. Its rule ends at the rail's edge: the rail's head draws none, in the frame or in the drawer.
anatomy.banner: Between the top bar and the content, not scrolling: a state that holds, such as the server not answering.
anatomy.content: The one scroller. A thin track (contentScrollbar) that keeps its room whether or not it scrolls.
anatomy.contentScrollbar: The content's scroll bar: a solid track whose room is kept.
anatomy.shellHead: A page header and tabs held above the scroller while the content scrolls.
anatomy.pageHeader: The page's head (parts/page-header): its title, what is known about it, and its actions. Held above the scroller with ShellHead. No trail: in the frame the page header states its trail for the top bar (trailInTop, its default there).
anatomy.page: The page's content at the page inset, its sections (parts/section) a page gap apart.
anatomy.pageState: What the page's read landed in, in the content's place: loading, failed, empty, or the content (parts/page-state).
anatomy.panel: An optional side panel (parts/side-panel): a column at the content's end from 1024, a sheet below it, or tabs in a strip at the foot. From 1024 up to 1280 the rail narrows to its icons while the panel is open, so the page keeps its room.
anatomy.panelToggle: A side panel's toggle in the window's top-right corner: over the top bar's end while the panel is closed or a sheet, in the panel header's corner while it is a column and open.
anatomy.foot: The status line (parts/status-line), one row of fixed height, level with the rail's foot cell so the account and the status read as one bar. It draws the strip itself; the shell gives it the room and draws no strip of its own.
anatomy.palette: The command palette over the page on Mod+K (parts/command-palette): places, the screen's commands and the app's search.
anatomy.settings: The settings dialog over the page it was opened from, on its own route (parts/settings-dialog).
anatomy.appearance: Light and dark (the scheme) are chosen in two places only: Settings › Appearance (with the theme, the density and the text size) and the command palette's appearance commands. The account menu's Appearance entry opens Settings at Appearance; it holds no scheme rows of its own. Never a scheme toggle in the top bar or in the account menu.
anatomy.dialog: Every dialog over the page, the settings and shortcuts dialogs among them (parts/dialog).
anatomy.drawer: Below 768 the rail as a drawer from the top bar's menu button, drawn expanded, with the account.

rail.does: The rail (parts/rail): its groups are the app's places, data the same on every target, which the palette repeats.

railMode.does: A work page with list and detail panes asks for the rail narrowed or hidden while it is shown.

top.does: The top bar (parts/top-bar). A screen draws its own while it is mounted (ShellTop), or states only its trail (useShellTrail).

palette.does: The command groups; without them no palette.

panelStrip.does: Below 768 the panel's tabs stand in a strip at the foot.

banner.does: A banner under the top bar.

desktop.does: A desktop window with its title bar hidden: the top strip is the title bar and leaves room for the window's buttons.
desktop.sokkel-ui: Shell desktop; Electron hiddenInset, Tauri Overlay

panelToggle.note: Centered in the top bar's height, 8 from the window's end.

contentScrollbar.note: A solid track scrollbar-width wide (10) whose room is kept whether or not the content scrolls, so the page head above ends at the same edge. sokkel-ui draws it with scroller-thin (the scroll bar's own pseudo-elements, scrollbar-gutter: stable); egui's bars float over the content unless its scroll style is set solid at this width.

trafficLights.note: Room for the window's buttons at the strip's start, in a desktop window with its title bar hidden.

pageInsetWide.note: When the content box is 640 or wider.

panelSheetGap.note: The panel's sheet stops 48 short of the window's far edge.

sequenceWait.note: ms for the second key of a sequence.

cells.width: The window. Below md (90 columns) the rail is a drawer and dialogs fill the screen; from lg (120 columns) the side panel is a column.
cells.density: The blank row at the page's top, and between its sections, are there at regular and gone at compact; the status line's rule row likewise.

page.note: density.page-inset-wide or -narrow by the content's own width (640 px, 76 columns), at most 2 columns; one blank row on top at regular.

drawer.note: The rail's expanded width, at most the window less 4 columns, over the content; what the content under it shows is open (open-questions.md, T2).

cells.note: Top bar one row, then the rail and the page side by side, then the status line: parts/top-bar, parts/rail and parts/status-line hold their own cells.

does: The rail leaves the frame: the top bar's menu button opens it as a drawer over the content, drawn expanded whatever the app holds, with the account in it (parts/rail, state drawer).
A press outside the drawer, a link, Escape or a change of route closes it.
The top bar keeps only its last crumb, and its search field gives way to the palette's button, an icon a finger square (parts/top-bar, state phone).
The side panel is a sheet from the right; with panelStrip its tabs stand in a strip at the foot, each a finger tall, raising the panel as a sheet.

Dialogs fill the screen as sheets, with no edge or shadow (parts/dialog), and settings opens on its list of sections; a section shows its rows with a back button, and the footer stays clear of the home indicator (parts/settings-dialog). A ConfirmDialog stays a box sized to its words.
Menu, select, command and combobox rows and tabs are a finger tall; the account menu leaves out Keyboard shortcuts.
The frame keeps clear of the notch and home indicator by the safe-area insets.
The rail stands in the frame, expanded or collapsed as the app holds it.
The side panel is a sheet from the right, closed at the start.
The side panel is the right column, level with the top bar, open at the start.
Desktop is the main target: every story is written at full width first.

routes.settings: #/settings: the settings dialog over the page it was opened from. Back (or Done, or Escape) returns to that page; a link opening the app on #/settings draws the app's home under it.
routes.page: #/<place>/...: the page in the content; a change moves focus to the new page's heading and closes the drawer.

rest.means: A page shown in the frame.

hover.means: The pointer over the panel toggle.

focus.means: Keyboard focus on the panel toggle.

drawerOpen.means: Below 768, the rail drawn as a drawer over the page, the page out of reach.

settingsOpen.means: The settings dialog over the page, on #/settings.
settingsOpen.reached: an action the app gives it (a row in the account menu, a palette command) or a link to #/settings; the account menu's Appearance opens it at the Appearance section

paletteOpen.means: The command palette over the page.

panelOpen.means: The side panel is shown: a column from 1024, a sheet below it.

drawerOpen.note: elevation-pop under it and the scrim over the page; it slides in over motion-base.

rest.note: The track's ground and the thumb.

keyboard.does: Opens the command palette; a second press closes it, unless a command is running (parts/command-palette). On a Mac Ctrl+K opens it too.
keyboard.when: nothing but the top bar's search results stands over the page

keyboard.does: Closes the layer on top: palette, dialog, sheet, menu, drawer; focus goes back where it was.
Goes to a place, as the app binds it; the second key within a second, never heard in a field.
On #/settings: closes the dialog to the page it was opened from.

appText.places: The app's places are the rail's groups (parts/rail); the palette repeats them.
appText.pageTitle: Each page's title; the actions follow their context: on Runs the button is New, not New run.
appText.settings: Every section's and setting's title, description and keywords (parts/settings-dialog).

sokkel-ui: The window's width decides the frame (media queries at breakpoint-md and breakpoint-lg, 768 and 1024); the page inset decides by the content's own box (a cqi clamp).
Links are real anchors through LinkProvider, so a middle click opens a tab; routes are hash routes in the examples.

useOverlayRoute (hooks/use-overlay-route) draws #/settings over the page it was opened from: it reads the app's route and goes back through the history and the hash, or through the app's own back and replace with a client router.
useOverlay makes the page inert under an overlay; useScrollMemory keeps each page's scroll; the safe-area insets pad the frame.
In a desktop shell (Electron, Tauri) the top strip is the window's title bar.
Shell's routeKey moves focus to the new page's first visible h1 after a route change, waiting up to 3000 ms while the page loads and until the reader presses a key or the pointer.

Every control of the frame (the rail's entries, its mark, home link and head control, the top bar's menu button, crumbs and palette's button, the panel toggle, the account control) wears the button's own focus look: a 2px ring outline 2 off, on keyboard focus only.
sokkel-egui: The window's width is the available rect; the page inset picks wide or narrow by the content rect, since a cqi clamp is CSS-only.
There are no URLs: a route is app state with a back stack; #/settings is the state settings-open with the page under it kept.
Overlays: egui's Modal for dialogs and the drawer, Popup for menus; the page under them must refuse input.
A native title bar can stay; a hidden one is the top strip, with egui's ViewportCommand::StartDrag.
A route change may move focus to the new page's heading as the frame sees fit; the wait is the renderer's own.

drift.today: As of sokkel-egui 1a87987: Shell lays out the Rail, the TopBar and the StatusLine (each with its own spec and drift) with the rail's foot cell level with the status line, PageHeader and PageState (each with its own spec and drift), Section, SettingsDialog with appearance settings and setting rows, Dialog, Select and the tooltip, DropdownMenu, CommandPalette on Mod+K, the drawer on a phone, the side panel (Shell::panel with SidePanel, parts/side-panel) and the banner in its slot (parts/banner); the account menu offers Appearance and no scheme rows of its own (5a0158e). Every widget names itself to a screen reader. Working apps run on it, with settings over the page on Mod+comma and from the rail. Not yet: the panel's toggle in the corner, and settings as a route: egui has no URL, so the dialog is open state the app holds. The page's scroll gutter is 11, where the spec proposes 10.

As of b99664f, drawn from the spec in cells, with the side panel (Shell::panel, on side-panel.base.rest.panel) and the banner's slot (on banner.{tone}.rest.container). Not yet: the shell's rule of contract 0.31.0 (light and dark chosen only in Settings › Appearance and the command palette, principle 9), the status vocabulary (index.json statuses), words keyed by their message ids, what lies under the drawer flattened under its scrim (T2), and the panel's toggle as this spec draws it.
